evidence.locator: write to `$3456` is the same as a write to `$2006`
evidence.claim: The PPU register ports mirror every 8 bytes across $2000-$3FFF, which is why this program's writes to $2006/$2007 are the canonical addresses rather than the only ones.
Sprite data reaches OAM through the DMA port at $4014, the mechanism this program uses to update its sprites each frame.
The PPU renders 256x240, which is the frame dimension this proof compares.

note: The NES has no boot ROM, so this proof has no restricted input and runs its execute stage in public CI as well as locally — the only machine here whose rendered frame is checked on every push.
evidence_caveat: ⚠ ALL EVIDENCE HERE IS DERIVED, NOT PRIMARY. Every other proof in this repo cites a period manual held in reference/by-system/. The NES has none: its by-system directory holds only this library's own authored .md references and a 587-character stub. Citing our own writing is materially weaker than citing Nintendo or a period book, and this proof should be re-grounded when a primary NES source is acquired. The tier field on each item records the distinction.
